# self-update: docker: invalid reference format with Docker CLI 29

Make `self-update docker` and the Docker helpers in `bin/lib/docker.bash` stop depending on the human-readable table of the Docker CLI. **Motivation:** after Docker CLI 29 changed the `docker images` table, `self-update` prints one `invalid reference format` per local image and still reports "Docker images were updated", so no image is ever refreshed. The same symptom as [[DOT-284]], with a different cause.

```
$ docker images --all
IMAGE            ID             DISK USAGE   CONTENT SIZE   EXTRA
golang:1.27      3680233e3204       1.32GB          320MB
node:22-alpine   c610fcdfb1d5        229MB         58.5MB

$ docker images --all | tail -n +2 | grep -v '<none>' | awk '{print $1":"$2}'
golang:1.27:3680233e3204
node:22-alpine:c610fcdfb1d5
```

The first column already holds `name:tag` and the second is the image id, so every pulled reference is `name:tag:id`.

Scope — every place that parses table output instead of asking for fields with `--format`:

- `update_docker` in `bin/self-update` — the list of images to pull;
- `images pull` — the same list; it also calls `images pull` recursively (the fault recorded against [[DOT-233]]);
- `volumes clean` — the volume name taken as the second column of `docker volume ls`, with an unanchored 64-character match;
- `images clean` — dangling ids passed to `docker rmi` as one quoted argument.

Acceptance: each list comes from `--format` (`{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}}`, `{{.Name}}`), and an empty list runs no Docker command on either BSD or GNU `xargs` ([[DOT-419]]).

Out of scope: the `image`/`volume` verb interface ([[DOT-232]], [[DOT-233]]) and reclaiming space after a pull ([[DOT-413]]).
